metadata.title: Young Citizens’ Views and Engagement in a Changing Europe
metadata.venue: IEA International Civic and Citizenship Education Study 2022 European Report

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This European report is based on ICCS 2022, which uses a complex, multi-stage sampling design to obtain nationally representative samples of Grade 8 (or Grade 9 when the Grade 8 average age is below 13.5) students and their schools. The report states that more than 66,000 students and about 33,000 teachers from about 2,800 schools participated across the participating European education systems, with both computer-based and paper-based administration depending on country. The excerpt provided does not specify the exact student weight variable names (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used; therefore, the weighting approach cannot be confirmed from the text shown. For ICCS analyses, analysts should apply the official ICCS sampling weights and, where provided, replicate weights when estimating standard errors and confidence intervals for scale scores and subgroup comparisons.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variables in this European report are questionnaire-based attitude and engagement scales (e.g., European identity, opportunities to learn about Europe, attitudes toward freedom of movement, discrimination perceptions, and expectations for the future), which are not described here as PV-based cognitive achievement outcomes. ICCS questionnaire scales are typically scaled using IRT-based procedures rather than PV generation for cognitive domains, so PV handling is not applicable for the reported constructs in this excerpt. Missing-data handling procedures are not provided in the excerpt, so the specific strategy (e.g., deletion vs. imputation) cannot be verified from the text shown.

data.outcome_summary: This ICCS 2022 European report summarizes results from a regional student questionnaire module administered after the international student questionnaire, taking about 15 minutes. The European student questionnaire was designed to measure affective and engagement constructs in a European context, including students’ sense of European identity, opportunities to learn about Europe at school, attitudes toward freedom of movement and restrictions within Europe, perceptions of discrimination, endorsement of environmental cooperation, political consumerism and sustainable behaviors, attitudes toward cooperation among European countries and the EU, and expectations for the future of Europe and students’ own future. The target population follows ICCS conventions: Grade 8 students (approximately age 14) unless the Grade 8 average age is below 13.5, in which case Grade 9 is targeted. Across participating European education systems, the report draws on data from more than 66,000 students and about 33,000 teachers from roughly 2,800 schools, with both computer-based and paper-based administration depending on country. The excerpt does not provide model-based ML results; instead, it reports scaled questionnaire outcomes and subgroup comparisons, with detailed scaling and equating procedures referenced to the ICCS 2022 assessment framework and technical report.
